title: Potato, French Fries, from Fresh, Baked

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato fries are made from fresh potatoes cut into sticks and baked in the oven without excessive oil. They retain the natural potato flavor, have a crispy exterior and a soft interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baked fries contain fewer calories than traditional deep‑fried versions.
Potato is one of the world’s most consumed vegetables, grown in over 100 countries.
Baking preserves more vitamins, especially vitamin C, compared with frying.
There are many seasoning options: paprika, garlic, rosemary, parmesan.
In Russia, “home‑made” oven fries are a popular side dish.

items.title: Rich source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are high in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C in fresh potatoes acts as an antioxidant and supports the immune system.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Baked fries contain significantly less fat than deep‑fried ones, making them more diet‑friendly.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: The skin of the potato provides dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high GI, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Excessive added salt to fries can increase the risk of hypertension.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Cooking at very high temperatures can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen; bake at 200 °C and avoid over‑drying.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked fries are served as a side dish with meat, fish, or as a snack on their own. Sprinkle with favorite spices and dip in sauces such as ketchup, yogurt, or mustard. For extra crispness, pat the cut sticks dry and lightly coat with olive oil before baking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked baked fries in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven to retain crispness. Raw potato sticks can be kept in cold water for up to 24 hours to prevent discoloration.
